description: The process every forger project starts from: the work-loop config, the process doc, the backlog and the ticket, PR, report and retro shapes.

opinions.summary: Every decision a ticket adds lands as a tested command with machine-readable output, not as prompt text.
Comments say why, never narrate a change; history belongs in the commit.
Prose, code and commits use ASCII punctuation only.

Docs and code carry no emails, home paths or terms on the project's denylist; addresses under hosts reserved for documentation and testing (RFC 2606, RFC 6761) are not reported, and a project that wants them reported denylists the domains.
Shipped instructions reach a skill only through a skill slot, never by name.
Prose names roles, not models or vendors; the adapter docs and the config name them.
Durable docs carry no counts, timings or dates; they point at the command that computes them.
One ticket per iteration, one feat PR carrying code, tests and docs.
Commands merge only through the merge tool, which waits for every check and refuses a red PR.

The harness hook refuses a worker's hand merge, push to the base branch or force push, status write, edit of the engine's state and a write or cd into the loop's checkout outside the worker's worktree; dropping a default rule needs a waiver.
A diff does not loosen a guard file, delete a guard or test file or skip a test unless the ticket's Decisions name it.
Gates are green before every commit and merge, and hooks are never bypassed.
